en: to be forced; to be pressured; to be coerced

examples.ko: 저는 회사에서 매일 야근을 강요당해서 힘들어요.
examples.en: I'm forced to work overtime every day at my company, and it's hard.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 공부를 강요당한 기억이 있어요.
examples.en: I remember being pushed to study when I was little.
Nobody was pressured; they chose by themselves.

examples.ko: 동의하지 않는데 사과를 강요당하면 화가 나요.
examples.en: It makes me angry to be forced to apologize when I don't agree.

examples.ko: 학생들이 특정한 생각을 강요당하는 일은 없어야 해요.
examples.en: Students should never be forced to accept a particular idea.
He said he was forced to move.

explain: 남이 시켜서 하기 싫은 일을 억지로 해야 하는 쪽을 말해요. '강요하다'는 시키는 쪽, '강요당하다'는 당하는 쪽이에요. '시키다'와 달리 싫은데 억지로 할 때만 써요.

phrases.en: My parents do not force me to study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시키는 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person doing the forcing.

phrases.en: I was pressured by my friend to go along.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강요당하다'와 비슷하게 당하는 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 강요당하다, said from the side of the person forced.

phrases.en: I did the thing I did not want to do against my will.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않는데 할 수 없이 한다는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy expression for doing something unwillingly.

explain_en: It names the person who is made to do something unwanted. '강요하다' is the side doing the forcing, '강요당하다' the side receiving it. Unlike '시키다', it is only for things done unwillingly.

p.n: 강요되다 has no 에게-agent; the lie itself is the subject.

examples.en: My friend changed their name this year.

examples.ko: 법원에서 허락을 받아야 개명할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can change your name only with the court's permission.
After changing my name, I am called by the new one.
My name is hard, so I plan to change it.
The singer became more famous after changing their name.
I looked into the documents needed to change my name.

explain: 법적으로 이름을 바꿀 때는 '개명하다'를 써요. '이름을 개명하다'는 뜻이 겹쳐서 어색하니 '개명하다'만 쓰는 게 자연스러워요. 가수나 배우가 활동 이름을 바꾸는 건 '예명을 바꾸다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 이름이 마음에 안 들어서 개명하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I don't like my name, so I want to change it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 바꾸고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you wish to legally change your name.
phrases.en_equiv: to want to change one's name

phrases.example: 개명한 뒤에는 새 이름으로 불러 주세요.
phrases.en: After I changed my name, please call me by the new name.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 뒤에'를 붙여 이름을 바꾼 다음의 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -ㄴ 뒤에 talks about what happens after the name change.

phrases.en: I applied for a name change at the court.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개명하다'와 달리 명사로 서류를 내는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for the paperwork of applying to change a name.

explain_en: Use '개명하다' for a legal name change. '이름을 개명하다' repeats the meaning and sounds awkward, so just say '개명하다'. For a singer or actor changing a stage name, say '예명을 바꾸다'.

examples.en: This broadcaster is state-run.
State-run companies are operated by the government.
State-run hospitals tend to have low fees.
That country runs its railways as a state enterprise.
In the past, many companies were state-run.

examples.ko: 그 나라의 국영 방송 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the news on that country's state broadcaster.

explain: 반대말은 '민영'이고, '국영 기업', '국영 방송'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸며요. 한국의 KBS처럼 공공이 운영하는 방송은 '국영'이 아니라 '공영 방송'이라고 해요. 다른 나라나 옛날 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: That country only has state-run broadcasting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정부가 운영하는 방송을 말하고, 주로 다른 나라 이야기에 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broadcasting run by the government; mostly used for other countries.

phrases.en: That company is state-owned, so it is stable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라가 주인인 회사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a company owned by the state.

phrases.en: This hospital is privately run, not state-run.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '민영'과 함께 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare with the opposite word 민영 (privately run).

explain_en: The opposite is '민영', and it modifies the next word: '국영 기업', '국영 방송'. A publicly run broadcaster like Korea's KBS is called '공영 방송', not '국영'. It often comes up when talking about other countries or the past.

examples.en: The government spokesperson made an announcement today.
The company spokesperson did not answer the question.
The spokesperson's words were published in an article.
The players chose a spokesperson for the group.
The reporter requested an interview with the spokesperson.
I passed on the opinions as the student council spokesperson.

explain: 단체나 회사의 공식 입장을 전하는 사람이에요. '○○ 대변인'처럼 이름 앞뒤에 직함으로 붙여 써요. 비슷한 '대표'는 단체를 이끄는 사람이라 달라요.

phrases.en: I saw the spokesperson's announcement on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대변인이 공식 입장을 말하는 것을 가리키는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair referring to an official statement by a spokesperson.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 올해 회사 대변인이 되었어요.
phrases.en: That person became the company spokesperson this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 그 일을 맡게 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone took on the role newly.

phrases.en: The reporter asked the spokesperson a question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기자회견 이야기에서 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in stories about press conferences.

explain_en: A person who conveys the official position of an organization or company. It is used as a title, as in '○○ 대변인'. The similar '대표' is the person who leads the group, so it is different.

examples.en: I got a copy of my resident registration at the dong office.

examples.ko: 이사한 뒤 전입 신고를 하러 동사무소에 갔어요.
examples.en: After moving, I went to the dong office to report my new address.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 동사무소는 여섯 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The dong office in my neighborhood closes at six.
A dong office employee helped me fill out the papers.
I wait for the bus in front of the dong office.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동사무소에서 하는 한글 교실을 다녔어요.
examples.en: As a child I attended the Korean-letters class held at the dong office.

explain: 지금은 공식적으로 '주민센터'나 '행정복지센터'라는 이름으로 바뀌었지만, 많은 사람이 습관처럼 아직 '동사무소'라고 불러요. 서류를 뗄 때는 '동사무소에 가다'라고 편하게 말해요. 새 이름도 대화에서 함께 들려요.

phrases.example: 이사한 뒤에 주민센터에서 전입 신고를 했어요.
phrases.en: I filed my change-of-address report at the community center after I moved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 공식 이름이라서 안내문이나 뉴스에서 '동사무소'보다 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the current official name, so it appears more often than 'dong office' in notices and the news.

phrases.en: I'm going to the neighborhood office to get a document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 뗄 때 습관처럼 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common habitual phrase when you need to get a document.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the neighborhood office

phrases.example: 동사무소 직원이 서류 쓰는 방법을 친절하게 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: The neighborhood office staff kindly showed me how to fill out the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to talk about the people who work there.

explain_en: The official name has changed to 주민센터 or 행정복지센터, but many people still call it 동사무소 out of habit. When you go to get a document, 동사무소에 가다 is the casual way to say it. The new names are heard in conversation as well.

examples.en: My passport expires next month.
The transit card's validity period expired yesterday.
Please contact me before the contract expires.

examples.ko: 쿠폰 유효기간이 만료돼서 쓸 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The coupon had expired, so I couldn't use it.
You can't pay with an expired card.

examples.ko: 이 이용권은 올해 말에 만료될 거예요.
examples.en: This pass will expire at the end of this year.

explain: 기간이 정해진 것(여권, 계약, 카드, 쿠폰)이 끝날 때 써요. 같은 일을 사람이 주어로 말하면 '만료하다'를 쓰는데 훨씬 드물어요.

phrases.en: The coupon's usage period has expired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 기간이 끝났을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for a set period ending.

phrases.en: My visa will expire soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝날 날이 가까울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the end date is near.

phrases.en: Be sure to check the expiration date of your passport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여권, 계약, 카드처럼 기간이 정해진 것이 끝나는 날짜를 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the date when something with a set period, like a passport, contract or card, ends.

explain_en: Use it for things with a set period, such as passports, contracts, cards, and coupons. 만료하다, with a person as the subject, is much rarer.

examples.en: The police investigate the cause of the accident.
This case is being investigated now.
It is a matter the prosecutors have investigated since yesterday.
They widened the investigation to find the culprit.

examples.ko: 내일부터 경찰이 이 일을 수사할 거예요.
examples.en: The police will start investigating this from tomorrow.

examples.ko: 경찰이 수사해서 밝힌 내용을 뉴스에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw on the news what the police revealed after investigating.

explain: 경찰이나 검찰이 범죄를 조사할 때 써요. 학교나 회사에서 일의 이유를 알아보는 것은 '조사하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The police are investigating the case now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사가 아직 끝나지 않았을 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in the news when the investigation isn't finished yet.

phrases.en: The police are investigating thoroughly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠뜨리는 것 없이 자세히 조사한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means investigating carefully without missing anything.

phrases.example: 그 회사가 경찰 수사를 받고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company is under police investigation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사를 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요. 조사하는 쪽은 '수사하다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side being investigated. The investigators use '수사하다'.

explain_en: It is used when the police or prosecutors look into a crime. When a school or company looks into the reason for something, you say '조사하다'.

dis.h: police or prosecutors investigate a crime

p.n: 조사하다 also works and is broader; 수사하다 is specifically criminal.

examples.en: The witness testified truthfully in court.
I have to give a statement to the police about the accident.

examples.ko: 그는 자기 입장을 차분하게 진술하고 자리에 앉았어요.
examples.en: He calmly stated his position and sat down.
What he stated did not add up.

examples.ko: 피해자가 사실을 진술할 때 목소리가 떨렸어요.
examples.en: The victim's voice shook as they gave their statement.
May I state my opinion first?

explain: 경찰이나 법원에서 사실이나 생각을 말할 때 많이 써요. 명사 '진술'은 '진술을 하다', '진술이 엇갈리다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서 가볍게 말하는 것은 '말하다'예요.

phrases.en: I gave a statement in front of the police.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '진술'을 써서 말하는 방식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 진술 instead of the verb.

phrases.en: I have to write a written statement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진술한 내용을 적은 문서를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The document in which a statement is written down.

phrases.en: The two people's statements conflict.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 말이 맞지 않을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when accounts do not match.

explain_en: It is the verb used at police stations and in courts for stating facts or views. The noun goes in '진술을 하다' (give a statement) and '진술이 엇갈리다' (statements conflict). For casual talk, '말하다' is used instead.
